name: Eppley Airfield
before:
Nebraska's busiest airport, three miles north east of downtown Omaha on the west bank of the Missouri. It handles more arrivals and departures than every other airport in the state put together.

The terminals split by airline, which makes it easy to brief a client. The South Terminal and Concourse A take Alaska, Allegiant, American, Delta and Frontier. The North Terminal and Concourse B take Southwest and United, and the consolidated car hire facility is attached to it.

The airport is in the middle of the BuildOMA modernisation programme, which has already taken one gate out of service, so expect the layout to keep changing.

Public transport is thin. Metro Transit line 106 runs at rush hour on weekdays only, and Express Arrow intercity coaches to Norfolk call at the terminal. For most clients that means a car or a taxi.

Three runways serve the 2,650 acre site, which sits close to four interstates.
after:
Nebraska's busiest airport, a few miles north east of downtown Omaha. It handles more passengers than every other airport in the state put together.

The terminals split by airline, which makes it easy to brief a client. Alaska, Allegiant, American, Delta and Frontier use the South Terminal and Concourse A. Southwest and United use the North Terminal and Concourse B.

The airport is in the middle of its Build OMA modernisation, due to be complete in 2028 with a single security checkpoint for all passengers. Expect the layout to keep changing until then; the airport advises allowing extra time.

Public transport is thin. Metro Transit route 106 runs at rush hour on weekdays only. For most clients that means a car or a taxi.

Three runways serve the 2,650 acre site.
